name: Risograph print
means: Duplicator printing in two or three spot inks: each ink laid as its own flat coarse-grained layer, the layers misaligned by a hair, ink sitting ON the stock so highlights are bare paper, and the inks multiplying to a darker third colour wherever they overlap. Soy-ink colours are fluorescent and the coverage is patchy.
prose: a risograph print in two spot inks, fluorescent pink and teal, each ink laid down as a separate flat layer with visible coarse grain, the two layers misregistered by a hair so every edge doubles, the inks overprinting to a dark third colour where they cross, highlights left as bare uncoated paper, patchy uneven ink coverage and roller streaks
negative_add: photorealistic, smooth gradient, full colour, 3d, airbrush
works_for: No. Grain plus misregistration is precisely the texture class that boils, and the doubled edges will strobe. INFERRED, not measured.
note: WEAK, and the reason is inventory rather than prompting skill. LORAS.md records that this box holds zero general style LoRAs - two anime ones on the qwen base and nothing else - so risograph rests entirely on whatever the base model absorbed from the word, and what comes back is usually a vague pink-and-blue duotone with none of the print mechanics: no overprint multiply, no bare-paper highlights, no misregistration. REACH FOR THIS INSTEAD: render the art as flat_vector or screenprint_poster with a deliberately tiny palette, then build the riso qualities in the deterministic tier - a duotone grade in studio/looks/ plus a channel offset gives you misregistration exactly and repeatably. That is the same argument studio/looks/night.json makes about darkness, applied unchanged: prompting for riso asks the model for adjectives, offsetting a channel asks ffmpeg for a fact. NOT AVAILABLE on animagine.
verdict: On qwen it drew a riso-coloured rectangle over the photo; on the illustration engine, nothing. Misregistration and spot ink are print artifacts neither model has. A STYLE LoRA WAS TRIED AND FAILED: six settings on the qwen path - illustration-1.0-qwen-image at 1.0 and 1.5, qwen_image_modern_anime at 1.0 and 1.5, qwen_image_2512_storybook at 1.0 with and without its trigger phrase. Not one produced misregistration, overprint multiply, coarse flat grain or bare-paper highlights. What did change: at illustration 1.0 the riso-coloured rectangle vanishes and leaves a plain photograph, and at 1.5 the two spot inks arrive as fluorescent pink and teal accents inside the LoRA's own watercolour; under storybook-with-trigger the inks became the stripes of a scarf. The COLOURS are nameable so they arrive; the press mechanics are not, so they never do. The card's own advice stands: build riso in the deterministic tier.
